feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: 5 men arrested on terror charges near U.K. air base released on bail
entry.summary: Five men arrested on terror charges near a U.S.-operated air force base in England were released on bail Monday, as police investigate whether there is a link to Iran.

entry.title: Former U.K. counterterrorism official discusses alleged terror plot near air base
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel asks Nick Aldworth, a former U.K. counterterrorism national coordinator, about the investigation into a suspected bomb plot near U.S. operations at an air base in England.

entry.title: SpaceX's Starship reaches orbit for the first time
entry.summary: SpaceX's mammoth rocket, Starship, reached orbit for the first time on Monday. The mission was shorter than expected, but SpaceX completed its objectives as it develops the world's largest rocket.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Five men arrested on terror charges near U.K. air base released on bail, Trump administration rolls back fuel efficiency standards for new vehicles, prosecutors reopen Cornell fraternity rape case.

entry.title: Journalist recounts his Russian imprisonment on false espionage charges in new memoir
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich about his memoir, "This Cursed Beautiful Land," on his imprisonment in Russia on false espionage charges.

entry.title: A young sailor died by suicide. Her family blames health care gaps and long deployment
entry.summary: Jaimie Bethea, a 21-year-old mass communication specialist, had been deployed on the USS Fort Lauderdale for more than 11 months. She died by suicide in June.

entry.title: Montana among states instituting Medicaid work requirements early
entry.summary: In most states, people with Medicaid coverage will have to prove they're working, volunteering or studying, starting Jan. 1. But Montana is starting that early, and it's sowing confusion and anxiety.

entry.title: Lindsay Clancy returns to court for the first time since mistrial
entry.summary: A judge in Massachusetts will consider several motions, including one to dismiss the triple-murder case against Lindsay Clancy, after a mistrial was declared over a deadlocked jury.

entry.title: Pastor barred from returning to the U.S. works to lead his congregation from afar
entry.summary: Pastoring is an intense job. But what happens when a pastor is stuck thousands of miles away from his church –- with no hope of returning anytime soon?

entry.title: Trump administration says it's scaling back fuel efficiency standards for new cars
entry.summary: The Trump administration is weakening Biden-era fuel efficiency standards for new cars and trucks.
